title: A root CA of your own
summary: Create a self-signed root with the extensions a real CA certificate carries.

steps.title: Anatomy of a root certificate
body: A root is a self-signed certificate that is **allowed to issue**. Three extensions make that so:
var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=Dojo Root CA", key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
// 1. "I am a CA"  (certificateAuthority, hasPathLengthConstraint, pathLengthConstraint, critical)
// 2. "My key may sign certificates and CRLs"
// 3. An ID for my key, so children can point at it (their AKI)
`CreateSelfSigned` returns the certificate **with** its private key attached, which is what you need to sign children.
Roots are long-lived (here 20 years) because replacing one means touching every trust store that has it.

steps.prompt: Complete the root's extensions: it is a CA, the extension is critical, and its key may sign certificates.
steps.explain: Basic Constraints `(true, false, 0, true)` reads: CA yes, no path-length limit, (ignored limit), critical. The SKI is computed from the request's public key.

steps.prompt: Match each constructor argument of `X509BasicConstraintsExtension(a, b, c, d)` to its meaning.
pairs: is there a limit on CAs below it?
how many CA levels may sit below it
reject the certificate if this extension isn't understood

code: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=" + name, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
steps.explain: Self-signed, carrying its key, marked as a CA. `[Flags]` enums print their set flags in value order, lowest first: `CrlSign` (2) before `KeyCertSign` (4).

steps.prompt: You created a root with `X509BasicConstraintsExtension(false, false, 0, true)` by mistake. What happens when you try `req.Create(root, ...)` to issue an intermediate from it?
options: `Create` throws: an issuer whose Basic Constraints says it isn't a CA can't issue
It works, but browsers will reject the intermediate later
It works fine; Basic Constraints only matters for leaves
It silently sets CA:TRUE on the root
steps.explain: `CertificateRequest.Create` refuses up front with an `ArgumentException`. Even if you got such a chain from somewhere else, validators reject it with `InvalidBasicConstraints`.

steps.prompt: Your team's private root CA (made with code like this) will be trusted by every internal service. Where should its private key live afterwards?
options: Offline: exported once to an encrypted PFX or an HSM, locked away, used only to sign intermediates
In the source repository next to the code that created it, so the build can issue certificates
Nowhere: delete it, the root is trusted anyway
steps.explain: Anyone with the root key can mint a trusted certificate for any internal name. Keep it offline and let an intermediate do daily issuing. Deleting it works too, but then you can never issue a new intermediate.

steps.title: Create a root
prompt: Write `X509Certificate2 CreateRoot(string name)` that returns a self-signed root CA (with its private key):
- Basic Constraints: CA, no path length limit, critical
starter: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=" + name, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
solution: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=" + name, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
hints: Copy the pattern from the first card.
template: Dojo.Eq("has its private key", true, dojoRoot.HasPrivateKey);
Dojo.Check("Basic Constraints: CA, critical", dojoBc != null && dojoBc.CertificateAuthority && dojoBc.Critical, "add X509BasicConstraintsExtension(true, ..., critical: true)");

Dojo.Check("Key Usage includes KeyCertSign and CrlSign", dojoKu != null && dojoKu.KeyUsages.HasFlag(X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign) && dojoKu.KeyUsages.HasFlag(X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign), "add X509KeyUsageExtension(KeyCertSign | CrlSign, true)");
Dojo.Check("has a Subject Key Identifier", dojoRoot.Extensions.OfType<X509SubjectKeyIdentifierExtension>().Any(), "add X509SubjectKeyIdentifierExtension(req.PublicKey, false)");
Dojo.Eq("validates as its own trust anchor", true, dojoChain.Build(dojoRoot));

steps.title: A root that can only have one CA level
prompt: Real roots often limit the depth below them. Write `X509Certificate2 CreateStrictRoot(string name, int pathLength)`:
the same as `CreateRoot`, but Basic Constraints **has** a path length constraint of `pathLength`.
With `pathLength` 1 the root can sign intermediates, and those intermediates can sign only leaves.
solution: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=" + name, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
hints: Only the Basic Constraints arguments change.
template: Dojo.Check("Basic Constraints: CA, critical", dojoBc != null && dojoBc.CertificateAuthority && dojoBc.Critical, "add X509BasicConstraintsExtension(true, ..., critical: true)");

Dojo.Check("Key Usage includes KeyCertSign and CrlSign", dojoKu != null && dojoKu.KeyUsages.HasFlag(X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign) && dojoKu.KeyUsages.HasFlag(X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign), "add X509KeyUsageExtension(KeyCertSign | CrlSign, true)");
Dojo.Check("has a Subject Key Identifier", dojoRoot.Extensions.OfType<X509SubjectKeyIdentifierExtension>().Any(), "add X509SubjectKeyIdentifierExtension(req.PublicKey, false)");
Dojo.Check("path length constraint is 1", dojoBc != null && dojoBc.HasPathLengthConstraint && dojoBc.PathLengthConstraint == 1, "pass true and pathLength as the 2nd and 3rd arguments");
